source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 22 May 1952, p. 5 ("Borough Councils"); Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1952, p. 6
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: 'Larne—In Inver Ward, the only one in which there was a contest, three candidates were nominated for two councillorships. The result of the poll was:—A. H. Girvan, 293; J. W. Sandford, 251; not elected, J. L. Hogg (outgoing), 222' (BNL 22 May 1952 p. 5; OCR Glrvan, S&ndford, HOKZ)

note: Election of the Larne Borough Council, May 1952: one alderman and two councillors for each of the five wards, 15 seats. Sixteen nominations were received; the only poll, on Wednesday 21 May 1952, was for the two Inver Ward councillorships (Belfast News-Letter, 22 May 1952, p. 5). Every other alderman and councillor was returned unopposed (Larne Times, 8 May 1952, p. 5, which prints every nomination; 15 May 1952, p. 4). No party labels are printed. The only contest in Larne was for two councillors in Inver Ward; the other wards were uncontested and are not itemised.
